expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: 'A ticket that is past its due time and still not closed is overdue. Support agents need to find these tickets fast...'. File keeps 'Prefix: `TKT`.'. Non-goals list under 'The feature deliberately does not do these things:' with 6 items (no notify/escalate/reassign, no missed-target record, no change to TKT-005 hours or business hours, no near-due warning, no due-time display, no filter options). Not headed 'Non-goals', but it is a labelled non-goals list.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 6 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012 (check_run's items=12/16 count pre-existing headings too). All '### PREFIX-NNN: Title', zero-padded, no duplicates, testable_lines=0. Bodies 2-5 sentences; CLI-010 (5 sentences) and TKT-014 (3 sentences + example paragraph) are longer than typical.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-006 amended, 'has the word `OVERDUE` between the padded state and the title' with a table of example lines. Filter: CLI-010/TKT-016 'only the tickets that are overdue'. Order: TKT-016 'sorted by due time ascending... same due time ... ID ascending'. Exact due: TKT-014 'At its exact due time a ticket is not yet overdue.' Closed: TKT-014 'A `closed` ticket is never overdue'. Empty: CLI-010 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion; the exit-code-0 choice is also listed as an assumption in the in-spec open questions ('Exit code of `overdue`. Assumption: 0...') and questions.md Q3.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No function/class/module/file names in new criterion bodies (check_run impl_words=0; the only .py hits in the diff are the pre-existing 'Touching tickets.py or sla.py' column of the AGENTS.md table). Outcomes are CLI lines, stdout, exit codes.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is a condition, not a state. The help desk derives it from the due time of a ticket (TKT-005) and the time at which a command runs... the log never records it.' TKT-015: 'No event is appended.' CLI-011: '`ticketdesk overdue` appends nothing to the log'. No new event kind proposed. INV-001/INV-002 are not cited by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014 reuses TKT-005 due time ('a P1 ticket created at 09:00 is due at 13:00'). The amended CLI-006 keeps 'prints one line per ticket in ID order, see TKT-013' and adds the mark to the line, 'The lines for other tickets do not change.' The list order is not redefined; the interaction is stated through the retained ID-order sentence in the same criterion, not by an explicit 'order stays' sentence.
